subject.title: Decouple mode="session" from thread binding requirement

question: Should OpenClaw make non-thread persistent native and ACP `sessions_spawn` sessions a first-class supported contract, and what routing and lifecycle semantics should they have?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the fix changes session ownership, channel delivery, ACP inline delivery, cleanup, and follow-up routing rather than repairing a narrow implementation defect.

options.title: Define non-thread persistence
options.body: Approve an explicit contract for unbound persistent sessions and require one coordinated implementation across runtime, schema, docs, and tests.

options.title: Keep session thread-bound
options.body: Keep `mode="session"` tied to thread binding and narrow this issue toward docs, current-conversation bindings, or `mode="run"` guidance.

options.title: Split ACP from native sessions
options.body: Handle ACP non-thread persistence through a separate affinity-style contract while deciding native subagent persistence later.

recommendation.title: Define non-thread persistence
recommendation.body: Approve an explicit contract for unbound persistent sessions and require one coordinated implementation across runtime, schema, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent core thread-binding refactor history and current blame make this the best available routing owner for the product-contract decision.
